from: The two routes' examples, with agents_more, which the workspace's agent serves beyond them (how many of a session's agents it left out past the 50 it gives). The second session is a session and an agent whose effort is a number, a token budget, and agents left out. The workspace writes a number only for an agent's effort (a session's is its status line's level, or a chat's chosen one, read back from the session's record, which its own programs can write); the page reads a number for either as a budget. The tests' stand-in for the workspace's map (tests/session_map_stand_in.py) answers with these, and the page's fixtures are made from them; tests/test_workspace_map_served.py runs the same routes against the real agent.

sessions.title: the session's title, as the list shows it
sessions.model: the model the session last reported, or null

agents.name: its name, or else its description, cut to 80 characters

sessions.title: a session on a token budget, as the list shows it
sessions.model: the model the session last reported, or null

agents.name: an agent whose effort is a token budget
